title: Extended-state DMT trials yield encounters with sentient others
place_text: Imperial College London; University of California San Diego

tellings.quote: minutes. And And those volunteers are all coming back with reports of encounters with sentient others.

plain: Graham Hancock, a writer on ancient mysteries and consciousness, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that scientists at Imperial College London and the University of California San Diego are running trials in the 2020s with DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, keeping volunteers under its effects for extended periods rather than a few minutes. According to Hancock, the volunteers all come back reporting encounters with "sentient others," thinking beings they meet while under. He links this work to researchers Andrew Gallimore and Rick Strassman, and tells it because it would suggest such beings may be real in some sense.
